theory: An evaluation is an identified procedure applied to an explicit selection, with rows reconstructed from recorded runs. Pooling combines compatible evidence instead of assuming all historical scores are interchangeable.
instead_of: Trusting runner totals and pooling by model name would conceal procedure drift, changed environments, and duplicate samples.

absorption.rationale: Explicit selections fit; adaptive sampling requires new condition and denominator semantics.

world_mapping.rationale: Rows, conditions, baseline tiers and pooling identity describe different experimental facts.

abstraction.rationale: Contracts and readers separate concerns, while batch and staged outcomes need mode-specific reconstruction.

justification.rationale: The runner explains selected-entry staleness and pooling distinguishes it from current corpus identity.

honest_limits.rationale: Pooling reports counts and comparability limits rather than proving causal harness benefit.

rehearsals.requirement: Run an ordered list of selected entries
rehearsals.why: Selection preserves explicit order and refuses unknown names.

rehearsals.requirement: Spend extra repeats adaptively on hard entries
rehearsals.why: The pooling key assumes a declared repeat structure rather than a changing sampling policy.

rehearsals.requirement: Pool disjoint batches after corpus growth
rehearsals.why: Board self-consistency is separate from present corpus aggregate identity.
